chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from a man from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

Regarding the woman whose husband died while she was married to him, but he had not yet entered (consummated) with her, he said: Half the dower is for her, and she is entitled to inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.

key_terms.الدُّخُولِ: Consummation of marriage (entering into the marital bed)
key_terms.الصَّدَاقِ: Dower or dowry given to the wife

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a widow if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Safwan ibn Yahya, clarifies the tripartite legal status of a widow whose husband died prior to consummation, affirming her entitlement to half the dowry, full inheritance, and the observance of iddah. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling distinguishes the case from one where the husband dies after consummation, where the wife receives the full dowry, highlighting the significance of 'dakhel biha' (consummation) in determining financial rights. The inclusion of iddah underscores that while the marital bond is not fully realized for financial division, the legal connection remains sufficient to require the waiting period.
